mini-gradebook-capstone.label: Final Project: Build a Mini Gradebook
mini-gradebook-capstone.summary: Build one mini gradebook cumulatively: create the report header, read and total scores, track the highest score, calculate the average, classify the result, count passing scores, and polish the final report.

capstone-mini-gradebook.title: Polish the final mini gradebook
capstone-mini-gradebook.prompt:
Start from the exact working project. Keep all calculations and status logic, but polish the output into the final report by removing the preview-only `Total:` line and printing only these lines in order:

`Student: <name>`
`Scores entered: <count>`
`Highest score: <highest>`
`Average: <average>`
`Passing scores: <passing_count>`
`Status: <status>`
capstone-mini-gradebook.hint: Do not rewrite the calculations. Move the report output after the score processing and omit only the `Total:` line.

help.concept: The final capstone step is a refactor of presentation, not a restart: preserve working logic and shape the output contract.
help.hint_1: Keep the score loop, total, highest, passing counter, average, and status thresholds.
help.hint_2: The final runtime output must not contain a `Total:` line.

capstone-mini-gradebook.starterCode:
student = input().strip()
count = int(input())
print(f"Student: {student}")
print(f"Scores entered: {count}")

total = 0
highest = 0
passing_count = 0
for i in range(count):
    score = int(input())
    total = total + score
    if score > highest:
        highest = score
    if score >= 70:
        passing_count = passing_count + 1

average = total / count

print(f"Total: {total}")
print(f"Highest score: {highest}")
print(f"Average: {average:.1f}")
print(f"Passing scores: {passing_count}")

if average >= 90:
    print("Status: excellent")
elif average >= 70:
    print("Status: passing")
else:
    print("Status: needs practice")

cp-1-read-gradebook-header.title: Add the running score total
cp-1-read-gradebook-header.prompt: Keep the exact working header. Now read exactly `count` integer scores (each 0–100) with `for i in range(count)`, accumulate them in `total`, and print `Total: <total>`.
cp-1-read-gradebook-header.hint: Initialize `total = 0` before the loop and add each score inside it.

help.concept: This step adds repeated score input and a numeric accumulator without replacing the working header.
help.hint_2: After the loop, print the accumulated total.

print(f"Scores entered: {count}")

cp-2-add-score-total.title: Track the highest score
cp-2-add-score-total.prompt: Keep the header and total working. Add a variable named `highest` that remembers the largest score seen so far, then print `Highest score: <highest>`.
cp-2-add-score-total.hint: Scores are 0–100, so `highest = 0` is a valid starting value for this project.

help.concept: A running maximum changes only when the current score is larger than the best score stored so far.
help.hint_2: Inside the loop, update it only under `if score > highest:`.

cp-4-calculate-average.hint: Check the narrower 90+ case before the broader 70+ case.

help.concept: An ordered `if` / `elif` / `else` chain turns the numeric average into one mutually exclusive status.
